actionability.justification: The remedy gives a concrete behavioral directive (actually run the command/test/check and report the real output rather than guessing) that is directly checkable against future transcripts.

generality_without_vagueness.justification: It broadens from release-claims specifically to any completion or verification claim while still anchoring to concrete actions (run, report real output), avoiding a pure platitude like 'be careful' but risking some breadth by covering 'any task, fix, or claim as complete.'

leakage.justification: The remedy text is fully generic with no project-, incident-, or tool-specific nouns leaked from the evidence.

routing_fitness.justification: Given a single thin, generic incident and an existing overlapping claude-md rule (R2) plus a pending broadening proposal (R6) pointed at the same rule, revising R2 rather than minting a new skill is the cheaper, consistent choice, though the thinness of the evidence (one short quote) makes the broadened scope somewhat speculative.

trigger_quality.justification: Not a skill, so no formal 'Use when...' clause is required, but the rule embeds a clear activation condition ('before reporting ... complete — or whenever the user asks you to verify something') that is concrete enough to apply consistently.
